notes: Section 2.1 replaces coherence-factual-correctness-score with batch-single-deployment-target to avoid a definition-based question. Section 2.3 replaces azure-critic-feedback-revision-loop with agent-framework-critique-termination-history and azure-code-dispatch-rule-routing with agent-framework-edge-condition-response-object to test documented Python callback behavior. Section 3.1 replaces image-edit-multipart-upload with image-jpeg-output-compression because multipart exclusivity could not be verified for stable Azure OpenAI v1.

cards.statement: Python apps using Azure OpenAI v1 read Responses API answer text through response.output_text.
cards.explanation: The Python SDK exposes response.output_text as a convenience property for reading generated text. Applications using raw REST inspect the response's output items instead.
cards.appliesTo: Azure OpenAI v1; OpenAI Python SDK

source.title: Migrate Python apps from Azure OpenAI Chat Completions to the Responses API

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 apps pass previous_response_id to continue from a stored Responses API response.
cards.explanation: Set previous_response_id to the earlier response's id when creating the next response. Azure OpenAI uses that stored response to connect the conversation turns.

source.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cards.statement: A classic RAG app using Azure AI Search passes retrieved passages into the model's generation context.
cards.explanation: The application queries Azure AI Search, then includes the returned passages when it asks the deployed model to answer. Application code controls this handoff.

source.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in Azure AI Search

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 JSON mode validates generated fields against the schema described in the prompt.
cards.explanation: JSON mode targets valid JSON rather than conformity to a schema requested in the prompt. Azure OpenAI structured outputs provide schema enforcement.
cards.misconception: Requesting a schema in the prompt makes JSON mode enforce that schema.

source.title: How to use JSON mode with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: A Microsoft Foundry developer maps context as a plain string when running Groundedness evaluation.
cards.explanation: Join retrieved chunks into one string before mapping them to context. The Groundedness evaluator uses this supplied source material to assess the response.

cards.statement: Microsoft Foundry Relevance evaluation uses a reference answer as its scoring comparison.
cards.explanation: The Relevance evaluator compares a response with the user's query. Its data mapping uses query and response to judge how well the response addresses that request.
cards.misconception: Relevance evaluates responses by comparing them with a reference answer.

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 Global Batch accepts requests for different model deployments within one submitted job.
cards.explanation: A Global Batch job targets one model deployment. Submit separate files and jobs when requests target different deployments.
cards.misconception: A batch file can mix requests for different model deployments.

source.title: Getting started with Azure OpenAI batch deployments

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 Batch API returns completed responses in the same order as the submitted input lines.
cards.explanation: Match Azure OpenAI Batch API outputs to their input requests by custom_id. Output line position does not reliably identify the corresponding input line.
cards.misconception: Batch output positions correspond to input positions, so an application can zip the files together.

source.title: Getting started with Azure OpenAI batch deployments

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 structured outputs keep nullable properties in the schema's required list.
cards.explanation: A nullable property still appears as a key in structured output. Declare it required and include null in its type to represent an optional value.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI v1 structured outputs reject schemas with recursive references to their own definitions.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI structured outputs support recursive schemas through JSON Schema references. A schema can refer back to its root or to a definition that references itself.
cards.misconception: Azure OpenAI's supported JSON Schema subset excludes recursive references.

source.title: How to use structured outputs with Azure OpenAI

cards.statement: Foundry Agent Service can automatically execute an app's local Python function for a v2 prompt agent.
cards.explanation: Application code executes a requested custom function and returns its result. Foundry Agent Service receives the result to continue the prompt agent's response.
cards.misconception: A service-side prompt agent executes the application's local function body.

source.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: Foundry Agents v2 uses the tool's argument schema to validate the app's submitted function_call_output.
cards.explanation: FunctionTool.parameters governs the model's call arguments. An app can submit a string as function_call_output even when the input schema describes an object.
cards.misconception: An object schema for tool arguments also requires an object as the submitted tool result.

source.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: Foundry Agents v2 lets an app reuse a conversation ID to retain context across agent requests.
cards.explanation: Reusing the conversation ID supplies the stored conversation to the next agent response. The app preserves continuity by targeting the same conversation.

source.title: Build with runtime components in Foundry Agent Service

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 developer selects an uploaded knowledge store through FileSearchTool.vector_store_ids.
cards.explanation: The file search tool retrieves from the vector stores named in vector_store_ids. The uploaded files belong to those stores.

source.title: File search tool for Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app treats its Files API upload response as confirmation that file search ingestion has finished.
cards.explanation: File upload and vector-store ingestion have separate completion states. Wait for ingestion to complete successfully before querying the new file.
cards.misconception: A successful upload means the file is ready for retrieval.

source.title: File search tool for Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: Code Interpreter can fetch a public web page during execution in a Foundry Agents v2 sandbox.
cards.explanation: The Microsoft-managed Code Interpreter sandbox blocks outbound network requests. An app supplies needed data through another approved integration.
cards.misconception: The managed Code Interpreter sandbox has outbound internet access.

source.title: Use Code Interpreter with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry toolbox lets a Microsoft Agent Framework app share tools with a Foundry agent.
cards.explanation: Foundry toolboxes expose an MCP-compatible endpoint. Microsoft Agent Framework clients can consume the toolbox's tools through that endpoint.

source.title: What is Toolbox in Microsoft Foundry?

cards.statement: By default, SequentialBuilder passes prior input and response messages to the next agent in a Python workflow.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Agent Framework's SequentialBuilder forwards the preceding agent's full conversation. This gives the next agent both incoming context and generated responses.
cards.appliesTo: Microsoft Agent Framework for Python; SequentialBuilder
cards.volatilityNote: SDK releases can change the default message propagation of SequentialBuilder.

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app copies a function call's call_id into function_call_output when returning results.
cards.explanation: The function_call_output call_id matches the originating function call. That identifier associates the submitted result with the requested operation.

source.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents

cards.statement: A Foundry Agents v2 app uses response.id as approval_request_id when approving an MCP tool call.
cards.explanation: approval_request_id matches the mcp_approval_request item's id. This associates the approval decision with the requested tool operation.
cards.misconception: The enclosing response ID identifies the tool's approval request.

source.title: Connect agents to MCP server endpoints

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 app uses example user and assistant messages to guide the model's answer style.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI uses example exchanges as context for the current generation. The examples show the response style the application expects.

cards.statement: For gpt-5.6-sol in Azure OpenAI v1, text.verbosity controls the effort spent on reasoning.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.6-sol uses text.verbosity for visible answer detail. The setting changes conciseness, not reasoning effort.
cards.misconception: The requested answer detail determines how much reasoning the model performs.
cards.appliesTo: gpt-5.6-sol; Azure OpenAI v1 Responses API
cards.volatilityNote: Model-specific parameter support can change in later deployment versions.

cards.statement: For gpt-5.6-sol, Azure OpenAI v1 can return raw hidden reasoning through reasoning.summary set to auto.
cards.explanation: For gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning.summary requests a supported reasoning summary. The Responses API keeps the underlying reasoning text hidden.
cards.misconception: A reasoning summary exposes the model's complete private reasoning.
cards.appliesTo: gpt-5.6-sol; Azure OpenAI v1 Responses API
cards.volatilityNote: Reasoning-summary controls depend on the deployed model version.

cards.statement: For gpt-5.6-sol, Azure OpenAI v1 Responses API reserves reasoning tokens outside max_output_tokens.
cards.explanation: For gpt-5.6-sol, max_output_tokens covers reasoning and visible output together. Reasoning consumes part of that generation budget.
cards.misconception: Reasoning tokens use a separate budget beyond the output-token cap.
cards.appliesTo: gpt-5.6-sol; Azure OpenAI v1 Responses API
cards.volatilityNote: New model versions can change how output-token limits account for reasoning.

cards.statement: To combine reasoning with function tools, a gpt-5.6-sol app uses Azure OpenAI v1's Responses API.
cards.explanation: gpt-5.6-sol combines reasoning and function tools through the Responses API. Chat Completions tool calls require reasoning_effort set to none.
cards.volatilityNote: Tool and reasoning compatibility varies with the deployed model and API family.

cards.statement: An Azure OpenAI v1 app puts reusable prompt content before changing user input to improve cache reuse.
cards.explanation: Azure OpenAI matches cached prompt prefixes. Keeping the shared prefix identical lets repeated requests reuse earlier input processing.

cards.statement: For a prompt agent, Microsoft Foundry lets an engineer compare model-call and tool-execution span durations.
cards.explanation: A prompt-agent trace separates model operations from tool operations. Inspecting their spans helps an engineer locate the step responsible for a latency spike.
cards.appliesTo: Foundry Agents v2; prompt-agent server tracing

cards.statement: For a prompt agent, Microsoft Foundry stores trace telemetry in the conversation history used to generate responses.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Foundry sends prompt-agent traces to the project's connected Azure Monitor Application Insights resource. The telemetry store is separate from agent conversation history.
cards.misconception: Agent conversation history also stores the trace telemetry.
cards.appliesTo: Foundry Agents v2; prompt-agent server tracing

cards.statement: A Microsoft Agent Framework app reads the group conversation in termination_condition to stop writer-reviewer rounds.
cards.explanation: GroupChatBuilder passes conversation messages to termination_condition. The application checks review history and returns a Boolean decision to end or continue the loop.
cards.appliesTo: Microsoft Agent Framework for Python; GroupChatBuilder
cards.volatilityNote: SDK constructor and callback contracts can change in later releases.

source.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows Orchestrations - Group Chat

cards.statement: Microsoft Agent Framework gives an outgoing AgentExecutor edge condition the generated response text as a string.
cards.explanation: An AgentExecutor sends an AgentExecutorResponse to its outgoing edge condition. Routing code reads message.agent_response.text when it needs the generated text.
cards.misconception: A conditional routing callback receives the agent's plain response text instead of its response object.
cards.appliesTo: Microsoft Agent Framework for Python; AgentExecutor and WorkflowBuilder
cards.volatilityNote: SDK response types and workflow callback contracts can change in later releases.

cards.statement: The app can pass a reference image to GPT-Image-2 for a product photo edit.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 combines the supplied image with edit instructions.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app can request a hosted image URL as the output from GPT-Image-2.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 returns base64 image data that the app decodes.
cards.misconception: GPT-Image-2 returns hosted URLs.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app chooses JPEG output from GPT-Image-2 by setting output_format to jpeg.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's output_format selects the encoded image format.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2's output_compression setting controls PNG compression for the app's generated images.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's output_compression setting applies to JPEG output.
cards.misconception: PNG supports output_compression.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app can request several output images from GPT-Image-2 in one generation call.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's n parameter requests separate output images.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app can mark an edit target using opaque pixels in a GPT-Image-2 image mask.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2 inpainting targets areas marked by transparent mask pixels.
cards.misconception: Opaque mask pixels mark edits.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app chooses low quality for latency-sensitive image generation with GPT-Image-2.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's low quality setting favors lower latency.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: GPT-Image-2's Image Edit API rejects a JPEG image because of its input format.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's Image Edit API accepts JPEG input files.
cards.misconception: Editing requires PNG input.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: The app sets input_fidelity to high to preserve faces more accurately in a GPT-Image-2 edit.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's input_fidelity prioritizes matching reference-image features.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.

cards.statement: Azure OpenAI applies explicit-size restrictions to a GPT-Image-2 request with size=auto.
cards.explanation: GPT-Image-2's size=auto may bypass explicit-size restrictions.
cards.misconception: Auto sizing enforces explicit-size restrictions.
cards.volatilityNote: Model versions can change supported generation and editing controls.
